correctness.rationale: For every q>=1, each primitive necklace of length six has a unique lexicographically least cyclic representative, and each set of t used ordered symbols has a unique monotone normalization to {0,...,t-1}. Exactly all t^6 candidate tuples for t=1,...,6 are enumerated. Two independently written exact programs enumerate via primitive rotations and via stable last-to-first permutation respectively, agree on all 384 accepted normalized images and their cyclic-input-run labels, and reproduce the 10 partition cells. The binomial lifting across q is a proven bijection, and the fraction asymptotic follows from leading binomial coefficients. No statement for other input lengths is made.

originality.rationale: The closest primary result proves U_q(6)=4 with example images and an algorithm excluding three-run inputs, but does not state the counts of four-, five-, or six-run inputs or the complete Parikh-partition census. The earlier all-length construction provides existence and lower bounds, not exact length-six numbers. Precise implication comparisons, alternative last-to-first descriptions, and targeted public-record searches did not identify an equivalent count theorem. The existing appendix makes computational extraction feasible; this is recorded as a residual risk and is not misrepresented as logical independence.

value.rationale: Length six is the exceptional input length singled out by the sharpness theory for unclustered BWT amplification, where the general half-length lower bound is not attained. The result completely counts sources at each possible cyclic-run number for every ordered alphabet and determines their exact letter-multiplicity support. It exhibits the structural restriction to at most four active letters for optimal four-run sources and the asymptotic scarcity fraction 7/(2q^2), addressing a natural finer classification left after the published optimum and existence results.
